stories.title: More families rely on food pantries. A food drive in St. Lawrence County aims to help
stories.summary_or_snippet: Working families in St. Lawrence County are turning more to pantries in summer. Organizers cite school-meal gaps, transportation barriers, and rising gas and food costs.
stories.evidence_text: The article says the need really intensifies in July and August when kids don't have access to those school meal programs, and even many working families are increasingly turning to food pantries to keep food on the table. It also says local providers see transportation barriers in a very rural county like St. Lawrence, with distance between resources and access to resources, and that pantry partners have seen increases in the last couple of months as more working families rely on food pantries to supplement their budgets.
stories.pressure_summary: North Country Public Radio reported a food-access gap in St. Lawrence County, NY, affecting low-income households, rural residents.
affected_group_keywords: working-age adults without a college degree
stories.claim_supported: In St. Lawrence County, NY, Working families in St. Lawrence County are turning more to pantries in summer. Organizers cite school-meal gaps, transportation barriers, and rising gas and food costs.
stories.limitations: The source describes conditions in St. Lawrence County, NY, but it does not prove a broader regional trend.
